summary: Jampa Losang Panglung was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery and his Magister and doctorate at the University of Munich, later working in various research roles at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Jampa Samten works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1987) and later as Director (attested 2003–2004) and Professor (attested 2015, 2026) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jampal Kunzang Rechung is a scholar of Tibetology. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1980–1988) and as Deputy Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1982).

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Tsennyi Tulku Jampal Norbu, and he taught the 14th Dalai Lama and the 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies master. He succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo, studied under numerous teachers including Khenpo Thupten and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught figures such as Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo was a master in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Rigdzin Zangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught students including Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Jan A. Schoterman was an Indologist who completed his doctoral thesis at Utrecht University under supervisor Henk Bodewitz (attested 1982) and also studied under Jan Gonda.

Jan Chozen Bays is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner. Educated at Swarthmore College and UC San Diego, she studied under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada, founded Great Vow Zen Monastery, and served as its abbess around 2002.

Jan Christian Schaffert works in Indology and computational studies. He is attested in 2026 as a project collaborator (Mitarbeiter) and researcher (Bearbeiter) on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).

Jan E. M. Houben is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held positions at the Dutch Research Council (attested 1999), Leiden University (attested 2000–2002), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2009–2012).

Jan Fontein was a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin and held curatorial posts at the Rijksmuseum and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

Jan Gonda was an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Utrecht and Leiden Universities under Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff and Willem Caland, he held the Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and the Indology chair (1932–1976) at Utrecht University.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. After studying at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz, he served as professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).

Jan Jaworski was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw from approximately 1923 to 1927 under Stanisław Schayer and later studied under Jean Przyluski (~1928–1930).

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a Sinologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University and studied under Édouard Chavannes and Henri Cordier. He taught Chinese at Leiden University (1919–1954) and held visiting professorships at Columbia, Princeton, and Oxford.

Jan N. Bremmer is a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar. He earned his PhD through Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam, and he held faculty positions at Utrecht University (1974–1990) and the University of Groningen (1990–2005).

Jan Nattier is a Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology scholar. She completed her PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and held professorships at Macalester, Hawaiʻi, Stanford, Indiana University Bloomington, and Soka University.
